newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volatility up before data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index volatility up before data.

text.p: Index options volatility rose Thursday ahead of Friday's U.S. employment report for December, traders said.
"The last few times the unemployment report came out, they've pumped volatility on Thursday, and if the number is good the market heads up and if it's bad they crush it," one trader in Chicago said.
"It looks like this is exactly what's happening today," he said. "The puts are not going down."
Index put premiums were down as the underlying market rallied, but traders said they expected premiums to drop more.
The S&P 100 index .OEX was ahead 7.62 points, or 1.04 percent, at 740.84 at around 1430 CST/2030 GMT. It had reached a session high of 742.76.
The broader S&P 500 index .SPX gained 7.20, or nearly 1.0 percent, to 755.61 after reaching 757.68.
At the same time, the most active OEX put, the January 735, fell 1-7/8 to 7. The option, which had open interest of 8,463 through Wednesday, traded about 12,750 contracts.
The January 730 put, which traded 10,880 contracts, fell 1-3/4 to 5-1/4. Its open interest was 14,513.
On the call side, the two busiest OEX options were the January 740 and January 745, with volume of roughly 12,000 contracts and 11,870 contracts, respectively.
The January 740 rose 3-3/4 to 10-5/8 and the January 745 added 2-5/8 to 7-1/4. The January 750 call traded 10,635.
Traders said that volumes were up from recent sessions, but few large blocks or noteworthy trades had crossed.
"I don't see anyone doing anything out of the ordinary," one index options broker said. "There's been no excessive call volume or put volume."
He explained that with the market being so volatile, institutions and some trading firms were simply using daily moves to pick off quick profits, rather than employ longer term trading strategies.
Thursday's rallies more than erased sharp losses posted Wednesday, when the OEX lost 5.61 points and the SPX fell 4.82 points.
The bellwether Dow industrial average surged 80 points to 6,629 by Thursday afternoon after dropping 51 points Wednesday.
The options trader said he was not sure whether the pickup in volatility in the face of a rising market indicated investors were positioning themselves for a "bad" employment number on Friday.
"If it's a bad number, they'll knock stocks down huge and volatility will go up further," he said.
Economists in a Reuters poll on average expect a rise of 192,000 in December non-farm payrolls and a dip in the jobless rate to 5.3 percent from 5.4 percent.
Stronger-than-expected data could strike fear of rate increases into investors and roil the market, traders said.
